answer: Like a river carving a ridge over years, real history cannot be rushed: require each new identity to link a distinct, long-lived account on an unrelated public network — say, a code-hosting profile with years of signed commits — verified by a cryptographic proof only its owner can produce. An attacker launching a gale of fake identities would need to buy or fabricate years of genuine public history for every single one, which costs far more than spinning up a fresh key.
